```python
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/dogs_zurich.csv')

# Prepare data for visualization
breed_counts = df['Rasse1Text'].value_counts().head(10)
district_counts = df['KreisLang'].value_counts()

# Set up the matplotlib figure
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 1, figsize=(10, 12))

# Plot 1: Top 10 dog breeds
sns.barplot(x=breed_counts.values, y=breed_counts.index, ax=axes[0], palette='viridis')
axes[0].set_title('Top 10 Dog Breeds in Zurich')
axes[0].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs')
axes[0].set_ylabel('Breed')

# Plot 2: Dogs by District
sns.barplot(x=district_counts.values, y=district_counts.index, ax=axes[1], palette='muted')
axes[1].set_title('Number of Dogs by District')
axes[1].set_xlabel('Number of Dogs')
axes[1].set_ylabel('District')

# Adjust layout
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
```
